solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pop? It does, mainly for the young?

definitions.text: Pop? It does, mainly for the young?

parts.words: Pop? It does, mainly for the young?
parts.note: two readings run together: a sweet chewed by children that is blown up until it bursts with a pop, and a bouncy style of pop music aimed at teenagers

explanation.surface: A musing on whether pop music is chiefly a thing for youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' reads as music, and it is, but it is also what the chewed sweet does when its blown bubble bursts.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubblegum is both a chewy sweet loved by children and a label for lightweight teen pop music.

clue.text: Was on the fiddle, and bent

definitions.meaning: played a violin, drawing the bow across the strings
curved over, as a head inclined in respect

explanation.surface: Someone was cheating the books, and was crooked with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' is British slang for cheating, which suggests crookedness; here it is literally playing the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a fiddle means drawing a bow over it, and the same spelling is the past tense of bending low.

clue.text: Swine upset everyone after scrap in entertainment venue

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the word for scrap

parts.note: to scrap something is to bin it

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word for swine upside down so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a hog is a swine
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Pigs knock over the crowd after a fight at a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses HOG to GOH. 'Scrap' looks like a fight, but it is the verb to throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: A bingo hall is a building where people go for an evening of the numbers game, a kind of entertainment venue.

clue.text: Don't tie the knot in line, one with streaks in

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
veins are streaks of colour, as in marble
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice not to marry, given to a queue of someone streaked with colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run in clue order; the first 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohabit without marrying was once called this, the old idiom for an unwed couple sharing a home.

clue.text: Old slogan urging Labour folk to get cracking!

definitions.text: Old slogan urging Labour folk to get cracking!

parts.words: Old slogan urging Labour folk to get cracking!
parts.note: a famous British advertising slogan from the Egg Marketing Board; 'get cracking' hints at breaking shells and 'Labour folk' at workers having breakfast

explanation.surface: A political party's slogan urging its supporters to hurry up and get busy.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the British political party, but it just means working people. The slogan was a 1950s-60s British egg advertising campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the actual advertising catchphrase urging workers to breakfast on an egg before their day.

clue.text: I want your animal for grooming: line up!

indicators.note: grooming tidies and rearranges, so the letters of the preceding words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A pet owner asks for their animal to be handed over for grooming, then calls a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line up' looks like an order to queue, but it is a noun phrase: a rail line climbing a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A funicular or rack railway climbing a peak is a rail line that goes up the slope.

clue.text: Division eight? That's so far down!

parts.note: a department, abbreviated dept, is a division of an organisation
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at how low the eighth division of a league sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth measures how far something extends downward, the distance below a surface.

clue.text: County, once, had finally mounted challenge

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word had
in a down clue, mounted means the word for challenge is read upwards

parts.note: to defy is to challenge

explanation.surface: A former county once rose up against a challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' reverses DEFY to YFED. Dyfed was a Welsh county from 1974 to 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyfed is a former county of south-west Wales, abolished in local government reorganisation.

clue.text: Photo in bar oddly displaying Indian city

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third, fifth and so on letters of the words photo in bar

explanation.surface: A picture hanging in a pub happens to show an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Poona, now spelt Pune, is a large city in Maharashtra in western India.

clue.text: Success with series is an accident

parts.note: a hit is a success
and means with, joining two things
a run is a series, as of wins

explanation.surface: A claim that a hit show followed by a series is just luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit-and-run is a road collision in which the driver flees the scene.

clue.text: Restless native following women's vessel

indicators.note: the scrambled letters come after the abbreviation for women

parts.note: W is a standard abbreviation for women

indicators.note: restless means unable to stay still, so the letters of native are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An agitated local comes after a women's ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restless' makes INEVAT from NATIVE. 'Vessel' suggests a boat but is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine vat is a large container in which grape juice is fermented, so a vessel in the sense of a receptacle.

clue.text: Plain's high point, reservoir fed by river

parts.note: up describes the high position, the top

indicators.note: fed by puts the abbreviation for river inside the word for reservoir

parts.note: a font is a reservoir, as for holy water or lamp oil

explanation.surface: A description of a plain's summit and a reservoir supplied by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed by' puts R inside FONT to make FRONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being candid and open, speaking plainly, is the meaning of the adjective here.

clue.text: Cloth round middle of piping grabbed by girl

indicators.note: grabbed by means the word for piping is held inside the girl's name

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name
piping hot means very hot

explanation.surface: A girl grabs a cloth wrapped round a piece of pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piping' suggests tubes but means hot, as in 'piping hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the loincloth worn by Hindu men, wrapped about the waist and legs.

clue.text: Retired from tie on Thursday in triumph

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for triumph

parts.note: to win is to triumph

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another comes after it

parts.note: a draw is a tied match

explanation.surface: A team pulls out of a cup tie on Thursday after a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts DRAW after TH, and 'in' puts THDRAW inside WIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired person keeps to themselves, shy and reserved, which is what withdrawn describes.

clue.text: Shopper's right to go for large bottles?

indicators.note: the letter for large goes in place of the letter for right, swapped into the informer's word

parts.note: to shop someone is to grass on them, so a shopper is a grass, an informer

explanation.surface: A customer's entitlement to buy big bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopper' is British slang for an informer, one who shops (betrays) others: a grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass is the collective name for glassware such as bottles, as in a recycling bin for glass.

clue.text: Top grub, as served here?

indicators.note: served up as a dish, the words are mixed and presented anew

explanation.surface: Excellent food, of the sort you would be served in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges TOPGRUBAS, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a British pub known for high-quality restaurant food.

clue.text: Drops antiwar novel by "weak and feeble" woman

indicators.note: by puts the queen's initials beside the scrambled letters
novel means new, so the letters of antiwar are arranged afresh

parts.note: Elizabeth I said she had the body of a weak and feeble woman; her royal cipher is ER

explanation.surface: A pacifist novel is placed beside a frail woman's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' makes RAINWAT from ANTIWAR. ER stands for Elizabeth Regina; the quote is from Elizabeth I's Tilbury speech.
explanation.definitionFit: What falls as rain comes down in drops, and the water collected from it is this.

clue.text: Trend for each party to dismiss

parts.note: a wave is a trend, as in a wave of enthusiasm
a means for each, as in once a day
a side is a party in a dispute

explanation.surface: A fashion where every party is set to sack someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To brush off an objection or idea without serious consideration is to dismiss it.

clue.text: Old rulers vacated Tangier: one united with king in 1007

indicators.note: vacated empties the word Tangier, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the king's letter goes inside the Roman numeral

parts.note: 1007 in Roman numerals is MVII
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Ancient rulers left Tangier, one joining forces with a king in 1007.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside MVII to give MVIRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumviri were the three-man ruling boards of ancient Rome, like Caesar, Pompey and Crassus.

clue.text: Bile sapping energy and forbidding brilliance

indicators.note: sapping drains away, so the abbreviation for energy is taken out

parts.note: spleen is bile, ill temper
E is the physics symbol for energy
dour means forbidding, stern

explanation.surface: Bad temper drains one's energy and makes one grim, not brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sapping' removes an E from SPLEEN to leave SPLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificence, glorious brightness, a close synonym for brilliance.

clue.text: Something is vexatious about showing this?

definitions.text: Something is vexatious about showing this?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters found are read in the opposite direction
showing means on display within the words something is vexatious

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what is so annoying in displaying something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' finds NGISV across the words, and 'about' turns it round. In Britain, two fingers raised palm inward is an obscene insult, shown in irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-fingered rude gesture is a hand signal of contempt, made when vexed.

clue.text: Royal once having time in trip to see game with Gunners

indicators.note: with joins the gunners' abbreviation to the rest

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army

indicators.note: the abbreviation for time goes inside the word for a game-watching trip

parts.note: a safari is a trip to see wild game

explanation.surface: A former royal had a spell on safari, taking in a match with Arsenal.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal football club are nicknamed the Gunners, but here the Gunners are the Royal Artillery. Ras Tafari was Haile Selassie's name before coronation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ras Tafari Makonnen became Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia, so a royal of former times.

clue.text: Hawk close to window punctures balloon

indicators.note: punctures means the last letter of window pierces the word for hawk

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them

indicators.note: close to takes the end letter of window

explanation.surface: A hawk near a window bursts a balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' suggests a bird, but it is a street-trader's verb; 'balloon' is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to expand or bulge, which is what swelling means.

clue.text: Musician's very short slate

indicators.note: short means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, to assail

explanation.surface: A musician's extremely brief slate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slate' suggests a roof tile but is the verb to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian musical direction meaning extremely, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Heads of armoured division make it their own

indicators.note: heads of takes the first letters of armoured, division, make, it and their

explanation.surface: Tank commanders claim a captured position as their own.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to confess or acknowledge it, a sense shared with the answer.

clue.text: Volunteers to remove weeds from lake

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
to hoe is to clear weeds with a garden tool

explanation.surface: Volunteers set about clearing weeds from a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe is a large freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada on the California-Nevada border.

clue.text: Informally, offering some food to consume on ship

indicators.note: consume means swallow, so the food word takes in the other pieces

parts.note: a pie is some food
re means on, about, as in a letter heading
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: Food offered on board ship, described casually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to consume' puts RESS inside PIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressie is chatty British slang for a present, a gift or offering.

clue.text: One quiet after dash, and rather pale

indicators.note: the pieces for one and quiet come after the word for dash

parts.note: a dash is a tiny amount, a whit
I is the Roman numeral for one
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone goes quiet after rushing about, looking a bit pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' suggests a sprint, but it means a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means somewhat, so this is a colour only faintly white.

clue.text: Use of the computer workshop goes to West Indian

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means travelling right to left, so the computing workshop phrase is read backwards

parts.note: an IT lab is a workshop where computers are used

explanation.surface: Use of a computer room passes to a West Indian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Indian' looks like one phrase, but 'goes to West' turns ITLAB around and 'Indian' means an Indian meal, as in 'going for an Indian'.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a dish served in Indian-style restaurants in Britain, so an Indian in the sense of a curry meal.

clue.text: Sweet stuff good in celery, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A sweet flavour turns up unexpectedly in celery.
explanation.definitionFit: Glycerine is a sweet-tasting syrupy liquid, used as a sweetener in foods.
